dialogue.text:
Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent, and I'm here to help evaluate your neck swelling. Just so you know, I'm an AI assistant and this call is recorded for quality.

When did you first notice the swelling in your neck?
Good morning, Doctor. I first noticed the swelling about two months ago, and it's been getting bigger since then.
Two months with progressive swelling—that's important to know. Have you experienced any pain or tenderness in the swollen area, or does it feel comfortable?
No, there's no pain at all, Doctor. It doesn't hurt when I touch it or anything like that. It's just been growing but not bothering me in terms of pain.
That's helpful—painless swelling that's been gradually enlarging over two months. Have you noticed any changes in your voice, difficulty swallowing, or any breathing problems?
No, Doctor, I haven't had any trouble with my voice, swallowing, or breathing. Everything seems normal in that regard—it's really just the swelling itself that I've noticed.
Have you had any fever, weight loss, or night sweats over the past two months?
No, I haven't had any fever, and I haven't noticed any weight loss or night sweats. I've been feeling pretty normal otherwise, just concerned about this lump on my neck.
Have you noticed any other lumps or swelling elsewhere on your body, or has this been isolated to your neck?
No, Doctor, it's just this one spot on the back of my neck. I haven't noticed any other lumps or swelling anywhere else on my body.

Thank you for that detail. Let me request an ultrasound of your neck to get a clearer picture of what we're dealing with.

REQUEST TEST: Neck_Ultrasound

RESULTS: Based on the ultrasound of the neck, the findings show a well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature. This appears to be a defined, encapsulated structure with characteristics consistent with a cyst rather than a solid mass.

The ultrasound shows a well-defined cyst in the subcutaneous tissue of your neck—which is actually good news, as cysts are typically benign. Has anyone in your family ever had similar cysts or lumps that required treatment?
No, Doctor, I don't recall anyone in my family having anything like this. No one's mentioned having cysts or lumps that needed treatment as far as I know.

Given the ultrasound findings showing a benign cyst and your otherwise normal health picture, I have enough information to make my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign subcutaneous cyst of the neck (likely epidermoid or dermoid cyst based on imaging characteristics).
